answer: Something I make a conscious effort to do for the environment is reduce my use of single-use plastic. I started a couple of years ago, after seeing some genuinely [[alarming]] documentaries about ocean pollution. Around the same time, I noticed how much plastic was piling up along the banks of the Jamuna near my home, and it really hit me that this was not just a distant problem. Now I carry a reusable water bottle and cloth shopping bags everywhere, and I avoid plastic packaging wherever I can. Jute bags are easy to find in Bangladesh, so there is really no excuse. I have even persuaded my mother to take a basket to the market instead of coming home with a dozen polythene bags. I do it because I feel we all have a personal responsibility to protect the planet, however small our individual contribution. I am [[under no illusion]] that my efforts alone will solve the problem, but I believe change starts with individuals. Honestly, I think it is easy to feel helpless about huge issues like climate change, but taking small actions gives me [[a sense of agency]]. It also makes me more mindful of my consumption in general, and I think twice before buying things I don't really need. I feel genuinely good about doing my part, however modest. I think if enough people adopt these [[sustainable]] habits, the collective impact could be significant. It is a small change, but it lets me live with a [[clear conscience]].

followUps.q: Do your friends do the same?
followUps.answer: A few of them do, and some started after teasing me about my cloth bag. Most still use plastic without thinking, though, so I try to set an example rather than lecture anyone.

followUps.q: What else would you like to do for the environment?
followUps.answer: I would like to join a riverbank clean-up group, as some young people organise them in our area. Planting a few trees on my grandparents' land in the village would also be a [[worthwhile]] project.

note: Added plastic on the Jamuna banks, jute bags and persuading his mother; plain-ish 'responsibility' and 'helpless' marks moved to [[under no illusion]] and [[a sense of agency]], added [[clear conscience]].
